claim: "What were the cursed 'poteaux carrés' of the 1976 final?" — "poteaux carrés" literally translates as "square posts", and the correct option is the only one describing square goalposts; the three distractors (concrete pillars, back four, steel gates) are implausible. q: In Saint-Étienne folklore, what were the cursed 'poteaux carrés' of the 1976 final?
o: The square-section goalposts and crossbar that twice denied Les Verts
The concrete pillars blocking views in the away end
A nickname for the opposition's back four
The steel gates the team bus got stuck behind
answer: The square-section goalposts and crossbar that twice denied Les Verts

claim: Temporal clause implies a direct rename: "originally carried which name, before being renamed after a football administrator in 1991". The stadium was Stadio Giovanni Berta (1932-1945), then Stadio Comunale for 46 years (1945-1991), and only then Stadio Artemio Franchi. The stem omits the intervening name and reads as if Berta ran to 1991.
q: Fiorentina's 1931-built home stadium originally carried which name, before being renamed after a football administrator in 1991?
